articles.title: Fibula fracture is associated with high rate of vascular injury among low velocity ballistic tibia fractures.
articles.authors: Wilson JC, Randhawa AS, Mace WS, Dallas-Orr D, Tse S, Fitzpatrick E, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients aged 18 years or older with low-velocity ballistic tibia fractures treated surgically
articles.sample_size: 34 patients (11 with tibia-fibula fractures, 23 with isolated tibia fractures)
articles.outcomes: Vascular injury on CT angiography and compartment syndrome requiring fasciotomy
articles.take_home: Patients with gunshot wounds to the shin who also had a broken fibula were much more likely to have blood vessel injury (73% versus 9%) compared to those with just a tibia fracture. The risk of compartment syndrome was higher in the fibula fracture group but the difference was not statistically significant.

articles.title: Implant size distribution and mid-term outcomes of transfibular total ankle arthroplasty in a Japanese cohort.
articles.authors: Yano K, Ikari K, Koseki T, Tominaga A, Okazaki K
articles.population: Japanese patients undergoing total ankle arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 50 patients (51 ankles)
articles.outcomes: Clinical outcomes using SAFE-Q questionnaire and ankle range of motion; radiological parameters including tibial angles and alignment; implant survival rate; complications including wound healing and fractures
articles.take_home: Transfibular total ankle arthroplasty produced good results in Japanese patients, with 98% of implants surviving at three years. Smaller implant sizes were predominantly used and proved adequate for Japanese patients' bone anatomy.

articles.title: Association of polyethylene type with revision and dislocation risk following primary total hip arthroplasty: a population-based cohort study from the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register.
articles.authors: Chabaita M, Iljazi A, Sorensen MS, Eriksson F, Overgaard S, Petersen MM
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 48,618 patients from 2000 to 2016
articles.outcomes: All-cause revision, dislocation, and cause-specific revision (dislocation, infection, aseptic loosening) according to polyethylene type and femoral head size
articles.take_home: Highly cross-linked polyethylene showed lower risks of dislocation and revision compared with standard polyethylene for implants with larger femoral heads (36 mm and 32 mm), but made no difference for smaller 28 mm heads. The benefits were modest and the study design means caution is needed before drawing firm conclusions.

articles.title: Global Perspectives on the Care Gap in Fragility Fracture Management: Bridging Evidence and Clinical Practice.
articles.authors: Tabu I, Armstrong E, Costa ML, Frihagen F, Magaziner J, Lee JK, et al.
articles.study_type: Narrative review and quality improvement synthesis
articles.population: Patients with fragility fractures globally, across high-income and low- and middle-income countries
articles.outcomes: Quality of fragility fracture care measured against evidence-based standards including timely surgery, orthogeriatric care, early mobilisation, weight-bearing tolerance, and secondary fracture prevention
articles.take_home: Fragility fracture care falls short of recommended standards worldwide, but the problem in poorer countries is mainly due to health system limitations rather than lack of evidence. Evidence-based care standards can be successfully adapted to different settings if health systems are strengthened and quality improvement programmes are properly implemented.

articles.title: Interlocking plate compared with conventional pin fixation for undisplaced femoral neck fractures: a randomized controlled trial with radiostereometric analysis.
articles.authors: Hogevold M, Hansen MM, Brattgjerd JE, Rohrl SM
articles.study_type: Randomized controlled trial with radiostereometric analysis
articles.population: Patients with undisplaced femoral neck fractures recruited from emergency departments
articles.sample_size: 25 patients randomized (12 pins, 13 plates); 17 completed 52-week follow-up
articles.outcomes: Fracture motion measured by radiostereometric analysis, Harris Hip Score, EQ-5D questionnaire, Timed Up and Go test, pain and satisfaction scores, reoperation rates, complications
articles.take_home: Interlocking plates provided better rotational stability than pins during healing of undisplaced femoral neck fractures, but this did not translate into better clinical outcomes or lower complication rates. The practical benefit of improved rotational stability remains unclear.

articles.title: Factors associated with surgical site infection after ankle fracture fixation: a retrospective study in northern Sweden.
articles.authors: Topalhafizoglu S, Stralmark J, Lundqvist R, Wanman J, Pietz G
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for ankle fracture
articles.sample_size: 781 patients
articles.outcomes: Incidence of surgical site infection within 30 days after surgery or up to 1 year with implant present; factors associated with infection including smoking, initial external fixation, and operative time
articles.take_home: Surgical site infection occurred in 11% of patients after ankle fracture surgery. Smoking, initial external fixation before definitive surgery, and longer operative time were associated with higher infection risk, suggesting that smoking cessation and efficient surgery planning may help reduce infections.

articles.title: Association of treatment method with mortality and functional outcome in patients with displaced femoral neck fracture: a cohort study of 60-69-year-old patients from the Swedish Hip Fracture Register.
articles.authors: Campenfeldt P, Hedstrom M, Olofsson O, Modig K, Al-Ani A
articles.population: Patients aged 60-69 years with displaced femoral neck fracture
articles.sample_size: 3,325 patients
articles.outcomes: 1-year mortality, 4-month functional outcomes (independent living and outdoor walking ability)
articles.take_home: Total hip replacement was associated with lower mortality compared to hip replacement with just the ball part or internal fixation, particularly in older or less healthy patients. Total hip replacement also helped patients maintain independent living and walking ability, especially in younger or healthier patients in this age group.

articles.title: Nordic hip fracture registries: comparisons toward a minimal common and standardized Nordic Hip Fracture Dataset (Nordic-HFD).
articles.authors: Schmidt CR, Palm H, Viberg B, Hedstrom M, Wolf O, Rogmark C, et al.
articles.population: Hip fracture patients in Denmark, Norway, and Sweden
articles.outcomes: Feasibility of creating a standardised Nordic Hip Fracture Dataset by comparing data variables across four national hip fracture registries
articles.take_home: Researchers found it is feasible to create a standardised hip fracture dataset across Nordic countries using existing national registry data, identifying 30 variables that could be harmonised across Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. Some variables like mobility and complications data need further work to ensure consistent definitions across countries.

articles.title: Pectoralis major reference technique improves humeral height restoration and tuberosity healing after hemiarthroplasty for complex proximal humeral fractures: A comparative study.
articles.authors: Park BS, Kim DH, Sohn HJ, Cho CH
articles.population: Patients undergoing hemiarthroplasty for complex proximal humeral fractures
articles.sample_size: 39 patients (24 conventional technique, 15 pectoralis major reference technique)
articles.outcomes: Complete tuberosity healing rate, head-tuberosity distance, humeral height restoration, pain scores, shoulder function scores, range of motion, rotator cuff insufficiency, complications
articles.take_home: Using the pectoralis major reference technique during shoulder replacement surgery for complex upper arm bone fractures led to better bone healing at the fracture site and improved shoulder rotation compared to standard surgical technique. Both methods were similarly safe, but the new technique more accurately restored the normal anatomy of the shoulder.

articles.title: Hip arthroplasty following proximal femoral tumour resection in children : the impact of age and articulation on implant survival and the outcomes following acetabular revision.
articles.authors: Baird CAE, Green N, Evans S, Kurisunkal V, Parry MC, Stevenson J
articles.population: Children aged 2 to 16 years with malignant proximal femoral bone tumours treated with endoprosthetic reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 60 patients (41 hemiarthroplasty, 19 total hip arthroplasty)
articles.outcomes: Revision-free implant survival, modes of implant failure, outcomes following acetabular revision
articles.take_home: Younger children (aged 12 years or under) have poor implant survival regardless of implant type, with half failing within five years. Older teenagers receiving total hip arthroplasty have better survival than those receiving hemiarthroplasty, though there is a small early risk of dislocation.

articles.title: Locking plate fixation compared with tension-band wiring for patellar fractures: a multicentre randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Larsen P, Thorninger R, Severinsen RP, Beuke JC, Jensen SS, Rasmussen MK, et al.
articles.study_type: Patient and assessor-blinded multicentre randomised controlled trial
articles.population: Adults with a displaced patellar fracture requiring surgical treatment
articles.sample_size: 122 patients (63 locking plate fixation, 59 tension-band wiring)
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: knee function at 12 months using KOOS (Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score). Secondary outcomes: hardware removal, fixation failure, and need for reoperation.
articles.take_home: Locking plate fixation resulted in better patient-reported knee function than tension-band wiring at 12 months, with greater improvements in symptoms, sport and recreation ability, and quality of life. Patients treated with locking plates also needed fewer reoperations and had fewer fixation failures.

articles.title: Five-year survival and complications of more than 300 articulating high-dose antibiotic spacers in two-stage revision total hip arthroplasties for infection.
articles.authors: Weintraub MT, Midthun WR, Pagnano MW, Taunton MJ, Sierra RJ, Mabry TM, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing two-stage hip replacement surgery for chronic joint infection
articles.sample_size: 298 patients (302 hip replacements)
articles.outcomes: Five-year reinfection-free survival, rerevision rates, dislocation, fracture, and Harris Hip Score
articles.take_home: This antibiotic-releasing spacer used during two-stage hip replacement for chronic infection had an 89% success rate at five years with no return of infection. Dislocation and fracture of the spacer each occurred in about 5% of patients, and spacer dislocation significantly increased the risk of hip dislocation after final implant, suggesting patients with this complication may benefit from more stable bearing designs.

articles.title: Patient-evaluated functional outcome is systematically different from physician-evaluated outcome after proximal humerus fracture fixation.
articles.authors: Sahu D, Chaubey A, Shah D
articles.population: Patients who underwent locking plate fixation of displaced proximal humerus fractures
articles.sample_size: 74 shoulders in 72 patients (mean age 56 years, 56% male)
articles.outcomes: Constant-Murley score (physician-evaluated), shoulder subjective value (patient-evaluated), pain scores, range of motion, and shoulder strength at minimum one-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Doctors and patients often disagree about how well the shoulder is working after fracture surgery, with doctors rating outcomes higher than patients do. Shoulder pain was the main factor linked to patients feeling their outcome was poor, whereas limitations in movement and strength were not.

articles.title: Patient, surgeon, and institutional variation in dual-mobility component use in primary total hip arthroplasty : a retrospective cohort study using data from the National Joint Registry Study.
articles.authors: Zucker BE, Howard JT, Whitehouse MR, Judge A
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement in England
articles.sample_size: 238,455 primary hip replacements (7,032 with dual-mobility components)
articles.outcomes: Variation in dual-mobility component use explained by patient, surgeon, and institutional factors
articles.take_home: The type of hip replacement component used varies much more depending on which surgeon and hospital treats you than on your individual patient characteristics. This suggests that current practice may not be based on sound evidence of who really needs this type of component.

articles.title: Effects of Capacity-Related Delay to Hip Fracture Surgery on Mortality: A Matched-Cohort Study.
articles.authors: King SW, Wakefield SM, Giannoudis VP, Relton SD, Giannoudis PV, Pandit HG, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity-score matching
articles.population: Adults aged 65 years and over treated for hip fracture at a UK teaching hospital
articles.sample_size: 2,358 eligible patients (1,087 with timely surgery, 1,271 with capacity-related delay)
articles.outcomes: Mortality at 30 days and 365 days after hip fracture surgery
articles.take_home: Hip fracture patients whose surgery was delayed due to lack of operating capacity had a higher risk of death within one year compared to those who had timely surgery, with the greatest difference seen in the first 30 days and among frailer patients. The study suggests that prioritising timely hip fracture surgery for vulnerable patients may improve survival.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of interventional radiology versus operative management in hemodynamically stable and unstable moderate-to-severe high-grade blunt renal trauma.
articles.authors: Hus A, Indorewala Y, Nasef H, Prashar S, Rogers L, Nasef Y, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over with moderate-to-severe high-grade blunt renal trauma
articles.sample_size: Not stated in abstract
articles.outcomes: Primary outcomes: mortality and nephrectomy rates. Secondary outcomes: transfusion requirements, nonoperative management failure, and complications.
articles.take_home: Interventional radiology was associated with lower death rates compared to surgery in patients with serious blunt kidney injuries, both in stable and unstable patients, with similar safety profiles. This suggests interventional radiology may be a preferable treatment approach for these injuries.

articles.title: Validity of fluoroscopic methods along the transsyndesmotic axis: A cadaveric study.
articles.authors: Nakajima H, Kimura S, Yamaguchi S, Watanabe S, Sasho T, Ohtori S
articles.population: Fresh-frozen cadaveric feet
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of three fluoroscopic methods (centre-centre, talar dome lateral, and incisura tangent) for positioning clamps along the transsyndesmotic axis, measured by angle and distance deviations, with and without metal implants present
articles.take_home: Two of the three fluoroscopic techniques tested (talar dome lateral and incisura tangent methods) were significantly more accurate than the centre-centre method at positioning clamps along the correct alignment for ankle syndesmotic injuries. Metal implants from fracture fixation did not affect the accuracy of any of the three methods.

articles.title: The epidemiology of motorsport injuries: Understanding crash dynamics in elite motorcycle racing.
articles.authors: Russo M, Bignami EG, Bitonti A, Valenti PG, Zasa M
articles.population: Elite motorcycle racing riders in the 2024 MotoGP season
articles.sample_size: 23 severe trauma cases extracted; all 2024 Grand Prix events analysed
articles.outcomes: Fall incidence, injury patterns by session type and bike category, severe trauma cases requiring medical disqualification or hospitalisation
articles.take_home: Sprint races and qualifying sessions had more crashes than practice sessions, and most serious injuries involved hands, wrists and collar bones from riders bracing during falls. Wet conditions at certain circuits increased injury risk further.

articles.title: Correlation of functional and radiological outcome after surgical treatment of acetabular fractures with quadrilateral plate involvement. A meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Solou K, Galanopoulos G, Lakoumentas J, Zacharakis E, Kyprianou A, Papachristos IV, et al.
articles.study_type: Meta-analysis of prospective and retrospective studies
articles.population: Patients with acetabular fractures involving the quadrilateral plate treated with open reduction and internal fixation
articles.sample_size: 336 patients across 12 studies
articles.outcomes: Functional outcomes measured by Harris Hip Score and Merle d'Aubigne and Postel score; radiological outcomes measured by MATTA score
articles.take_home: Good anatomic reduction on X-rays was associated with better hip function after surgery for complex acetabular fractures, particularly when reduction was excellent compared to poor. However, the relationship was not always strong, suggesting that achieving good positioning alone may not guarantee the best functional results and that secure fixation also plays an important role.

articles.title: Surgical rib fixation in pediatric patients: Following the adult trend or a different story?
articles.authors: Hamdan HS, Halabi M, Nouiri AE, Gardner C, Djuric M, Hill L, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national trauma database
articles.population: Children under 18 years with rib fractures
articles.sample_size: 28,465 pediatric rib fractures (87 treated with surgery)
articles.outcomes: Mortality, surgical fixation rates over time, injury severity, need for additional chest procedures
articles.take_home: Surgical rib fixation in children remains very uncommon (0.31% of cases) and has not increased over time, unlike in adults. It is used mainly in older children with severe injuries like flail chest, and those who had it had zero deaths compared to 7.3% in children treated without surgery.

articles.title: Delivery outcomes following previous pelvic ring injury: A systematic review, meta-analysis and evidence informed management pathway.
articles.authors: Gupta VK, Phua SN, Rai SK, Thakker A, Qayum K, Sanghera RS, et al.
articles.population: Women of reproductive age with previous pelvic ring injury
articles.sample_size: 1253 women and 1719 deliveries across 10 observational studies
articles.outcomes: Caesarean section rate, vaginal delivery rate, trial of labour success, preterm birth, neonatal intensive care unit admission, birthweight, perinatal mortality, chronic genitourinary symptoms and sexual dysfunction
articles.take_home: Caesarean section is more common after pelvic ring injury (40% compared to 60% vaginal delivery), but this varies widely between groups and often reflects patient and clinician preference rather than medical necessity. Most women with previous pelvic ring injury can safely attempt vaginal delivery, and having had surgery, retained implants or most types of fracture should not automatically mean caesarean section is needed.

articles.title: Beyond damage control: Functional preservation and avoidance of iatrogenic harm in combat vascular injury and fasciotomy.
articles.authors: Dmytro M, Ihor R, Iurii M, Serhii M
articles.population: Patients with combat vascular trauma and vascular injury
articles.outcomes: Appropriate use of damage-control interventions including temporary shunting, vessel ligation, endovascular management, and fasciotomy to balance lifesaving benefits against iatrogenic injury and long-term functional impairment
articles.take_home: Damage-control surgery for vascular injuries should be tailored to each patient's situation, with temporary shunts and selective interventions preferred over routine extensive surgery to reduce unnecessary harm. Major arteries should generally be repaired or shunted to preserve limb function, whilst prophylactic fasciotomy should be reserved for high-risk patients with prolonged lack of blood supply or combined injuries.

articles.title: Innovative intramedullary nail system with internally locking: A safe alternative fixation technique for humerus shaft fracture that reduces the risk of the iatrogenic radial nerve injury and surgical time.
articles.authors: Onder Y, Tuncez M, Kurtulus T, Bulut T
articles.population: Patients with humeral shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nailing
articles.sample_size: 75 patients
articles.outcomes: Operative time, hospital stay, radiological union time, return to activity, radial nerve injury, infection, Constant-Murley score, QDASH, VAS, shoulder range of motion
articles.take_home: This new intramedullary nail system for upper arm fractures achieved good results with an average surgery time of 46 minutes and no nerve injuries or infections in 75 patients. Patients typically returned to daily activities within 13 weeks and reported excellent arm function at follow-up.

articles.title: Splenic artery embolization versus surgery for blunt splenic injuries: a systematic review, meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis stratified by hemodynamic status.
articles.authors: Bravin S, Menegat ALRS, Menegat BLRS, Miron AM, Wiederkehr H, Garza EG, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients with blunt splenic injuries
articles.sample_size: 33,148 patients (9,593 treated with splenic artery embolization)
articles.outcomes: Mortality, length of hospital and intensive care unit stay, thromboembolism risk, and additional complications
articles.take_home: Splenic artery embolization (a minimally invasive procedure to block blood flow to the spleen) was associated with lower death rates, shorter hospital stays and lower risk of blood clots compared to surgery for blunt splenic injuries. These benefits were seen even in patients who were unstable at presentation.

articles.title: Pediatric digit replantation: A mixed methods outcomes study.
articles.authors: Saoud K, Bruce JG, Bettlach C, Tung TH, Fox IK
articles.population: Children aged 0-18 who presented to a Level 1 Trauma Paediatric Hospital with upper extremity trauma
articles.sample_size: 19 children underwent digit replantation or revascularisation; 12 digits survived to first post-operative visit; 10 patients and families interviewed
articles.outcomes: Digit survival to first post-operative visit, functional outcomes, school and sports participation, patient and parent satisfaction with surgery
articles.take_home: Most children who had digit replantation surgery had their finger successfully reattached and went on to use their hand normally at school and sport. However, some children and parents reported ongoing physical or emotional difficulties after surgery, suggesting the procedure is technically successful but can involve a challenging recovery.

articles.title: Anomalous occluded vessels and the "Corona Mortis": A reappraisal of nomenclature origins, anatomical variations, and surgical risks.
articles.authors: Song X, Wang F, Zhang Z, Zhang Q, Dong J, Wang J, et al.
articles.study_type: Narrative review of anatomical, imaging, and clinical literature
articles.population: Anatomical variations in pelvic vasculature across published studies, autopsies, and imaging reports
articles.sample_size: Multiple studies from 1996 to 2025; recent large-scale CTA studies referenced
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of corona mortis (approximately 50% of hemipelves); arterial and venous variant incidence; imaging detection rates; bleeding risk stratification; surgical management recommendations
articles.take_home: Corona mortis is a common anatomical variation found in about half of people, but it is not inevitably dangerous. The risk of serious bleeding during surgery depends on the size and exact location of the vessels, and can be managed effectively with proper planning and surgical techniques.

articles.title: External fixation for displaced intra-articular calcaneal fractures: A case series.
articles.authors: Morelli F, Caperna L, Pepino M, Iorio R, Maffulli N
articles.population: Patients with displaced intra-articular calcaneal fractures
articles.sample_size: 32 patients (35 fractures)
articles.outcomes: Time to partial weight-bearing, external fixator removal time, AOFAS functional score at final follow-up, infection and complication rates
articles.take_home: External fixation successfully treated displaced heel bone fractures, with most patients able to bear weight after about a month and remove the fixator after about three months, achieving good functional scores with few complications.

articles.title: Moderate accuracy of the AO/OTA Forearm Shaft Fractures Classification as used in the Swedish Fracture Register.
articles.authors: Berggren A, Wadstrom MG, Mukka S, Hailer NP, Wolf O
articles.population: Adult patients with forearm shaft fractures registered in the Swedish Fracture Register
articles.sample_size: 122 radiograph sets classified by three orthopaedic surgeons
articles.outcomes: Moderate accuracy of fracture classifications in the register (kappa 0.56); substantial to almost perfect agreement between expert raters (kappa 0.70-0.92); lower accuracy for B-type fractures (kappa 0.24)
articles.take_home: Forearm fracture classifications recorded in the Swedish Fracture Register showed moderate accuracy overall, though expert surgeons agreed well with each other. The system works poorly for certain fracture types with undisplaced wedges, suggesting guidelines need improvement.

articles.title: Analysis of factors associated with emergency airway intervention after extubation in patients surgically treated for traumatic cervical spinal cord injury without planned prophylactic airway management.
articles.authors: Ijuin S, Inoue A, Nishimura T, Tada K, Suga M, Kikuta S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with traumatic cervical spinal cord injury treated surgically, without planned prophylactic airway management
articles.sample_size: 221 patients
articles.outcomes: Emergency airway intervention after postoperative extubation. 23% of patients required emergency airway intervention. Risk factors identified: neurogenic shock, complete motor impairment, and vertebral artery injury.
articles.take_home: After surgery for cervical spinal cord injury, about 1 in 4 patients needed emergency airway support after being taken off the breathing tube. Patients with neurogenic shock, complete paralysis, or blood vessel injury to the neck were at much higher risk, with those having all three factors needing emergency airway support 100% of the time.

articles.title: Modified Delphi consensus recommendations for the use of negative-pressure wound therapy in orthopedic trauma and complex wounds in low- and middle-income countries: anAn African consensus study.
articles.authors: Manegabe JDT, Englebert A, Kabakuli AN, Buzisa Mbuku R, Tissingh E, Schubert T, et al.
articles.population: Orthopedic trauma and plastic surgeons from African countries
articles.sample_size: 40 experts (88.9% response rate from 45 invited)
articles.outcomes: 14 consensus recommendations on negative-pressure wound therapy use in orthopedic trauma and complex wounds in low- and middle-income countries; 2 achieved very strong consensus (≥90% agreement), 8 achieved strong consensus (80-89%)
articles.take_home: African experts agreed that negative-pressure wound therapy should be used alongside standard open fracture management, after thorough surgical cleaning, and followed by soft-tissue reconstruction. The recommendations provide practical guidance for using this treatment in resource-limited settings, though experts noted that some technical details need more research.

articles.title: Impact of altered consciousness on the risk of fasciotomy for acute compartment syndrome following traumatic tibial fracture.
articles.authors: Bouklouch Y, Poirier P, Parent-Harvey S, Esfahani SJ, McBeth K, Harvey EJ
articles.population: Patients with traumatic tibial plateau and shaft fractures
articles.sample_size: 119,393 patients with tibial fractures (6,854 underwent fasciotomy)
articles.outcomes: Fasciotomy rates during hospitalization in obtunded versus non-obtunded patients
articles.take_home: Patients with altered consciousness (sedation, intoxication, or low Glasgow Coma Scale) had a modestly increased likelihood of undergoing fasciotomy surgery for compartment syndrome following tibial fracture. This may reflect the difficulty in reliably assessing symptoms like pain in obtunded patients, potentially lowering the threshold for surgical intervention.

articles.title: Comparative performance of CRAMS, RTS, NISS, and ESI scores in predicting 24-hour mortality in adult multi-trauma patients: A prospective study.
articles.authors: Saznaghi FH, Hakimi H, Alizadeh A, Hosseinigolafshani S
articles.population: Adult multi-trauma patients presenting to emergency department
articles.sample_size: 265 patients (16 deaths within 24 hours)
articles.outcomes: 24-hour mortality prediction; NISS showed highest accuracy (AUC 0.98, sensitivity 100%, specificity 92.77%), followed by CRAMS (AUC 0.96), RTS (AUC 0.93), and ESI (AUC 0.88)
articles.take_home: Four trauma scoring systems all predicted early death in multi-trauma patients with reasonable accuracy, but the New Injury Severity Score (NISS) performed best. Using trauma-specific scoring systems rather than general emergency triage tools may help emergency staff identify high-risk patients more reliably.

articles.title: Pre-hospital paediatric preventable injuries: Who, what, when and where?
articles.authors: Kocierz L, Bird F, Henry CL, Strutt M, Dobbie A, Lockey DJ
articles.study_type: Retrospective review of pre-hospital trauma service data
articles.population: Children aged 16 years and under attended by a physician-led pre-hospital trauma service
articles.sample_size: 782 patients (607 with potentially preventable injuries)
articles.outcomes: Types and patterns of preventable injuries (falls from height, penetrating trauma, road traffic collisions), patient demographics, timing and location of incidents, association with socioeconomic deprivation
articles.take_home: Young children are most at risk from falls from height, whilst older children experience more penetrating injuries and road traffic accidents, particularly in early evening. Children in more deprived areas face significantly higher rates of all types of preventable injury.
